items.question: In a mixed-tier pipeline, which principle governs how tasks are assigned to tiers?

options.A: Match each stage to the minimum tier capable of meeting its quality requirement; escalate only where the lower tier demonstrably fails
options.B: Assign all stages to Opus for quality, then downgrade individual stages only if budget runs out
options.C: Use Haiku for all stages and accept lower output quality to control costs
options.D: Use the same tier for all stages to ensure consistent output behaviour across the pipeline

items.question: Extended thinking adds value when applied in combination with Opus primarily because:

options.A: Opus is the only tier that can activate extended thinking
options.B: Extended thinking and Opus together are cheaper than either alone
options.C: Opus's deeper base reasoning, combined with extended thinking's path exploration, addresses genuinely hard analytical problems more thoroughly than either provides alone
options.D: Extended thinking compensates for Opus's higher latency by pre-processing inputs

items.question: A team is deciding between Projects and one-off chats for a recurring monthly task. The deciding factor is BEST described as:

options.A: Whether the task requires an Opus-level model tier
options.B: Whether consistent context and custom instructions across sessions justify the overhead of maintaining a Project
options.C: Whether the task will be run by more than five team members
options.D: Whether Research mode is required for the task

items.question: A workflow enables extended thinking on every request, including simple ones. The MAIN inefficiency is:

options.A: Extended thinking produces lower-quality output on simple tasks than standard inference
options.B: Extended thinking disables Project knowledge when active
options.C: Simple tasks do not require path exploration, so extended thinking's reasoning tokens are wasted without improving the output
options.D: Extended thinking cannot be deactivated once enabled on a Project

items.question: An organisation is building an internal tool that requires automated execution, version-pinned model behaviour, and integration with an existing data pipeline. The correct surface is:

options.A: The Anthropic API, which provides the programmatic control, version pinning, and integration capability the tool requires
options.B: Claude.ai Projects, which can be automated through the web interface
options.C: Claude Code, which integrates with pipelines and supports version pinning
options.D: Claude.ai desktop with connectors configured by IT

items.question: A user consistently escalates model tiers when outputs are unsatisfactory, without revising prompts. This pattern MOST likely indicates:

options.A: The user's tasks genuinely require Opus-level reasoning across all domains
options.B: The user has identified the correct diagnostic sequence for quality problems
options.C: A misunderstanding that tier capability compensates for underspecified prompts
options.D: An organisation that correctly prioritises quality over cost

items.question: Which TWO are valid considerations when deciding whether to use Projects versus one-off chat for a task? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Projects always use a more powerful model tier than one-off chat
options.B: Projects are appropriate when instructions and reference materials need to persist across sessions
options.C: One-off chat is appropriate for isolated tasks that do not benefit from accumulated context
options.D: One-off chat provides larger context windows than Projects
options.E: Projects are only useful when a team of more than three people shares the workspace

items.question: Which TWO correctly characterise situations where using the Haiku tier in a mixed pipeline is appropriate? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The stage involves classifying or routing items where errors are low-cost and correctable
options.B: The stage requires synthesising ambiguous evidence into a nuanced strategic recommendation
options.C: The stage uses extended thinking to explore a complex analytical problem
options.D: The stage processes large volumes of identical structured inputs where Sonnet offers no measurable quality advantage
options.E: The stage produces the final client-facing deliverable that requires the highest available accuracy

items.question: Which TWO factors, taken together, most strongly justify switching from Claude.ai to the Anthropic API for a given workflow? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The workflow requires automated, programmatic execution without a human triggering each request
options.B: The user finds Claude.ai's interface less convenient than a terminal window
options.C: The workflow must be embedded in a product or automated pipeline that other systems call
options.D: The team has engineers available who could build the integration
options.E: The organisation's current plan tier does not include access to Claude Code

items.question: Which TWO statements correctly capture the relationship between model tier selection and prompt quality? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A well-crafted prompt at Haiku tier always outperforms a poorly crafted prompt at Opus tier
options.B: Escalating the model tier without improving the prompt often produces marginal gains because the prompt's ambiguity limits what any tier can achieve
options.C: Model tier selection matters more than prompt quality for determining output depth and relevance
options.D: Prompt revision should be attempted before tier escalation when output quality is unsatisfactory
options.E: Extended thinking compensates for a vague or underspecified prompt by exploring more possible interpretations

items.question: What are the five canonical building blocks of an effective prompt?

options.A: Role, context, task, constraints, format
options.B: System, user, assistant, context, format
options.C: Goal, audience, instructions, examples, style
options.D: Persona, background, task, tone, length

items.question: Which building block specifies the shape the output should take?

options.A: Role
options.B: Constraints
options.C: Context
options.D: Format

items.question: Which building block supplies background information the model cannot infer from the task alone?

options.A: Role
options.B: Format
options.C: Context
options.D: Constraints

items.question: What does the constraints building block primarily govern in a prompt?

options.A: Limits, exclusions, and content categories that must be omitted
options.B: The persona and expertise level Claude should project
options.C: The structure and shape of the output
options.D: Background facts Claude needs to understand the situation

items.question: What does the role block NOT do in a prompt?

options.A: Establish the persona Claude should adopt
options.B: Supply the situational background Claude needs to answer well
options.C: Calibrate the vocabulary and expertise register of the response
options.D: Signal the audience type to shape communication style

items.question: What is the primary benefit of stating success criteria explicitly within a prompt?

options.A: It removes the need to specify an output format
options.B: It prevents Claude from asking clarifying questions
options.C: It replaces the need to provide reference material
options.D: It gives Claude an internal standard to evaluate its own draft against

items.question: Which building block is the most direct lever for calibrating vocabulary complexity for a specific audience?

options.A: Context
options.B: Task
options.C: Constraints
options.D: Format

items.question: When should reference material be supplied verbatim in a prompt rather than described in the context block?

options.A: When the material is short enough to be paraphrased accurately
options.B: When the task requires reasoning against exact text, figures, or data
options.C: When the topic falls within Claude's training knowledge
options.D: When the task is iterative rather than single-shot

items.question: What is the effect of an explicit 'ask before proceeding' instruction in an ambiguous prompt?

options.A: It prevents Claude from making any assumptions during task execution
options.B: It directs Claude to request missing information before generating output
options.C: It routes the query to a higher-tier model automatically
options.D: It activates a structured step-by-step reasoning mode

items.question: What does increasing prompt specificity primarily reduce in Claude's output?

options.A: Output variability and interpretive guesswork
options.B: Token consumption
options.C: Latency for complex tasks
options.D: The probability of refusals on sensitive topics

items.question: Which statement best distinguishes the role block from the context block?

options.A: Role specifies output shape; context specifies content exclusions
options.B: Role instructs Claude's persona and stance; context supplies situational facts
options.C: Role sets audience calibration; context sets the task deliverable
options.D: Role constrains what Claude may generate; context defines quality thresholds

items.question: Which of the following instructions belongs to the constraints block rather than the format block?

options.A: Write the response as a numbered list
options.B: Keep all output under 150 words
options.C: Do not include speculative recommendations
options.D: Use H2 headings for each section

items.question: Output is well-structured but ignores the reader's technical level. Which building block most directly needs strengthening?

options.A: Format
options.B: Task
options.C: Role
options.D: Context

items.question: What is the primary function of few-shot examples in a prompt?

options.A: To teach Claude a concept it does not know from training
options.B: To trigger step-by-step reasoning before answering
options.C: To demonstrate the expected input-output pattern through worked examples
options.D: To increase the variety of outputs across repeated runs

items.question: What does a chain-of-thought instruction in a prompt primarily accomplish?

options.A: It causes Claude to produce multiple alternative answers for review
options.B: It makes Claude provide worked examples before attempting the task
options.C: It prompts Claude to externalise reasoning steps before reaching a conclusion
options.D: It automatically structures output using numbered sections

items.question: Few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting both improve output quality. Which statement precisely distinguishes their mechanisms?

options.A: Few-shot improves format accuracy; chain-of-thought improves factual recall
options.B: Few-shot increases output diversity; chain-of-thought constrains it toward a single path
options.C: Few-shot is used for classification tasks; chain-of-thought is used for generative tasks
options.D: Few-shot calibrates the output pattern through examples; chain-of-thought reduces reasoning errors by externalising steps

items.question: Which TWO of the following accurately describe few-shot prompting? (Choose TWO)

options.A: It works by demonstrating the desired input-output pattern through worked examples
options.B: It triggers the model to externalise its reasoning steps before concluding
options.C: Example quality and representativeness matter more than the number of examples
options.D: It is most effective for tasks that require multi-step logical inference
options.E: It substitutes for providing reference material when domain knowledge is needed

items.question: Which TWO of the following accurately describe task decomposition as a prompting strategy? (Choose TWO)

options.A: It involves breaking a complex task into smaller, sequentially executable sub-tasks
options.B: It is equivalent to chain-of-thought prompting because both involve multiple steps
options.C: It reduces the risk of errors compounding across a multi-step task
options.D: It requires all sub-tasks to be handled in a single prompt
options.E: It is most useful when a task can be completed accurately in a single pass

items.question: Which TWO of the following instructions are best classified as format directives rather than constraints or context? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Do not include legal disclaimers
options.B: Present the output as a two-column table with headers Risk and Mitigation
options.C: The audience consists of non-technical middle managers
options.D: Begin each paragraph with a bolded key term
options.E: Avoid any mention of specific vendors

items.question: Which TWO of the following symptom-fix pairings are correct? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Output uses vocabulary that is too technical for the intended audience — strengthen the context block
options.B: Output includes content from an excluded topic area — strengthen the format block
options.C: Output is formatted as a prose paragraph when a structured table was requested — strengthen the format block
options.D: Output approaches the task from the wrong expert perspective — strengthen the context block
options.E: Output ignores stated scope boundaries — strengthen the task block

items.question: What is the primary purpose of delimiters in a prompt?

options.A: To increase the model's reasoning depth on complex problems
options.B: To separate different content sections so the model does not blend instructions with source material
options.C: To specify the output format the model should use
options.D: To trigger structured chain-of-thought behaviour

items.question: What is prompt chaining?

options.A: Passing one prompt's output as the input to the next prompt in a sequence
options.B: Combining few-shot examples with chain-of-thought reasoning in one prompt
options.C: Breaking a complex task into smaller sub-tasks for separate prompts
options.D: Using identical prompts across multiple model tiers to compare outputs

items.question: What does the principle 'scope one prompt to one job' mean?

options.A: Each prompt should use exactly one building block from the five-block model
options.B: Each prompt should be submitted to exactly one model tier
options.C: Each prompt should be designed to accomplish one well-defined task rather than several simultaneously
options.D: Each prompt should contain exactly one example before the actual task

items.question: When a prompt contains a long reference document and a specific question, where should the question be placed?

options.A: At the beginning, before the document, to anchor the model's attention
options.B: Embedded within the document, at the point most relevant to the question
options.C: In a separate message, after the document has been submitted
options.D: After the document, so the model reads the full material before receiving the question

items.question: What is the primary risk of omitting delimiters between instructions and reference material in a prompt?

options.A: The model will refuse to process the prompt due to ambiguous structure
options.B: The model may treat parts of the reference material as instructions or vice versa
options.C: The model will produce output in the format of the reference material
options.D: The model will ignore the reference material and answer from training knowledge

items.question: Why is positive framing generally more reliable than negative framing when specifying desired output behaviour?

options.A: Positive framing specifies exactly what the model should do, whereas negative framing leaves the desired behaviour implicit
options.B: Negative framing triggers content refusals on sensitive topics
options.C: Positive framing uses fewer tokens, reducing latency
options.D: Negative framing is only processed in the constraints block

items.question: What makes a few-shot example representative for prompting purposes?

options.A: It is the longest example in the set
options.B: It is authored by the model rather than the user
options.C: It reflects the actual range of inputs the prompt will encounter in real use
options.D: It demonstrates the simplest possible case to keep the prompt short

items.question: When is task decomposition preferred over a single complex prompt?

options.A: When the task involves fewer than three steps
options.B: When the same model tier is used for all steps
options.C: When a single-shot response would reliably produce the full correct output
options.D: When errors in early steps would corrupt later steps if not caught and corrected

items.question: Which concept describes the design decision to split a complex task into sub-tasks, rather than the runtime mechanism of passing outputs between them?

options.A: Task decomposition
options.B: Prompt chaining
options.C: Chain-of-thought prompting
options.D: Multi-turn conversation management

items.question: What is the general relationship between the number of few-shot examples and output quality?

options.A: More examples always improve output quality linearly
options.B: Quality peaks at a small number of high-quality examples; adding more yields diminishing returns
options.C: A single example is always sufficient regardless of task complexity
options.D: Output quality is independent of the number of examples once format is clear

items.question: What additional benefit do XML-style tags provide over plain text delimiters such as triple backticks?

options.A: They enable the model to search the internet for content matching the tag label
options.B: They allow the model to execute the content within tags as code
options.C: They carry semantic labels that identify what each section is, aiding multi-document prompts
options.D: They prevent the model from generating content that contradicts the tagged material

items.question: Which statement correctly identifies task decomposition as a design concept rather than a runtime technique?

options.A: Decomposition is the planning decision to split a complex task into sub-tasks before any prompt is written or executed
options.B: Decomposition is the act of passing one prompt's output as the input to the next prompt
options.C: Decomposition is the technique of making the model reason step by step within a single response
options.D: Decomposition is the evaluation process of scoring each sub-section of a response separately

items.question: Why is a negative instruction such as 'do not be vague' generally less effective than a positive alternative?

options.A: Negative instructions increase token count without improving output
options.B: Negative instructions are processed after positive instructions and may be ignored
options.C: Negative framing removes a bad option without specifying which good option to use instead
options.D: Negative instructions trigger a refusal on topics marked as sensitive

items.question: What is the most likely consequence of providing few-shot examples that only show the simplest input cases?

options.A: The model will ask for clarification when it encounters harder inputs
options.B: The model will apply the demonstrated pattern incorrectly or fail on more complex inputs
options.C: The model will ignore the examples and default to its training behaviour
options.D: The model will produce shorter outputs than needed for complex inputs

items.question: For which task type does chain-of-thought instruction add the least value relative to its token cost?

options.A: Multi-step arithmetic with intermediate calculations
options.B: Policy application requiring several conditional inferences
options.C: Single-label classification of a short text into one of four categories
options.D: Diagnosing which of several possible causes explains a described system behaviour

items.question: How does a direct 'think step by step' instruction differ from a few-shot example that itself shows explicit reasoning steps?

options.A: The instruction relies on Claude's default reasoning; the example demonstrates the expected reasoning format
options.B: The instruction applies only to mathematical tasks; the example applies to any task
options.C: The instruction requires a longer output; the example keeps the output concise
options.D: They are functionally identical and produce the same output quality

items.question: Which TWO of the following are valid uses of XML-style tags in a prompt? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Triggering internet search for content matching the tag label
options.B: Separating instructions from reference documents to prevent blending
options.C: Executing code snippets placed within tags
options.D: Labelling multiple source documents so instructions can reference them by name
options.E: Automatically applying the tag's format to the model's output

items.question: Which TWO of the following correctly describe benefits of task decomposition? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Each sub-task can carry targeted instructions without overloading a single prompt
options.B: It eliminates the need for format instructions because sub-tasks are self-defining
options.C: Errors in early steps can be caught before they propagate to later steps
options.D: It reduces the total number of tokens consumed across the full workflow
options.E: It makes each sub-task equivalent in complexity to a zero-shot prompt

items.question: Which TWO statements correctly distinguish prompt chaining from task decomposition? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Decomposition is the design decision to split a task; chaining is the runtime mechanism that implements it
options.B: Chaining requires at least five steps; decomposition works with any number
options.C: Decomposition operates within a single prompt; chaining spans multiple prompts
options.D: Chaining passes the output of one prompt as input to the next; decomposition defines what each step should accomplish
options.E: Decomposition and chaining are synonymous; both describe the same multi-step process

items.question: Which TWO situations most strongly favour providing few-shot examples rather than a verbal task description alone? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task requires producing output in a precisely-defined format that is difficult to specify in words
options.B: The task requires factual knowledge the model does not have from training
options.C: The desired output has a consistent style or voice that is easier to demonstrate than to describe
options.D: The task involves a subject area beyond Claude's training cutoff
options.E: The task requires the model to refuse certain input categories
